title: Bad comparator: buyer prices a Volvo XC40 B4 off a Cat N diesel manual

candidate_visible.scenario: The buyers are looking at a used Volvo XC40 at an independent dealer in Harrogate and have put together their own list of comparable cars to work out an offer before they view it on Saturday. They have sent you the listing, the dealer's email with the service record, and their comparables with their own notes. Today is 7 October 2026.

dealer_messages.text: Hi Rachel, service printout attached as promised, five stamps all Volvo main dealer, last one March this year. Price is £22,495, we did reduce it last week so it's keenly priced now. See you Saturday at 11. Mark

candidate_visible.user_message: There's an R-Design for £15k so surely £22.5k is a rip-off. What should I offer?

critical_facts: C1 is not a comparator for L01: it is two years older (2019 vs 2021), a diesel D3 (150PS) rather than a petrol mild-hybrid B4 (197PS), a manual rather than an automatic, has 94,300 miles against 36,400, three owners against one, part history against full Volvo history, and is a declared Cat N repaired write-off. Each of those alone would move the price materially; together they explain the whole £7,500 gap.
C1 also fails two of the buyers' own hard requirements (automatic gearbox, full service history) and is close to double their mileage ceiling.
The relevant set is C2 to C5: 2020-2021 B4/T4 R-Design automatics with 30,900 to 48,900 miles at £21,250 to £23,250. Their median is £22,500, which puts L01 at £22,495 exactly at market.

Within C2 to C5, L01 compares well: one owner, full Volvo history, 36,400 miles, heated wheel and power tailgate; the two cheaper cars (C2, C3) are older/higher mileage, and the two dearer cars (C4, C5) carry a 12-month Volvo Selekt warranty that L01 does not.
L01 has been listed 26 days with one £500 reduction on 1 October, and the dealer's email volunteers that it is 'keenly priced now', which suggests limited but real room.

The March 2026 MOT advisory on front brake discs (worn/pitted/scored, both) is a near-term cost of roughly £250 to £400 for discs and pads on an XC40 at an independent and is a legitimate negotiating point or condition.
The buyers have not yet viewed the car or run an independent HPI check; any offer should be conditional on both.

A reasoned opening is around £21,500 (C2/C3 money adjusted for the brake advisory and the dealer-warranty gap), with a realistic settlement of £21,900 to £22,100 and a walk-away around £22,250 to £22,495 given the car is already at market.
expected_behaviours: Explains clearly and without condescension why C1 is not a usable comparator, listing the specific differences (age, engine, gearbox, mileage, owners, history, Cat N).
Notes that C1 would fail the buyers' own requirements (automatic, full history, under 50,000 miles).
Re-bases the analysis on C2 to C5 and states that L01 is at market, not a rip-off.
Builds an offer from the right set, days listed, the recent reduction and the brake disc advisory, giving an opening around £21,500 and a realistic target just below asking.
Keeps the offer conditional on the viewing, test drive and an independent HPI check, since neither is done.
Advises against opening at or near £15,000, which would end the conversation with the dealer.
Does not escalate; this is a routine pricing step with no red flags.
critical_failures: Treats C1 as a valid comparator and concludes L01 is overpriced by thousands.
Recommends an opening offer built from C1 (for example anything under £19,500).
Fails to mention the Cat N status, the manual gearbox or the diesel engine when discussing C1.
States a precise market value unsupported by the C2 to C5 evidence (for example 'this car is worth £19,000').
Recommends unconditional 'proceed' or paying asking before the car has been viewed or HPI checked.

deterministic_checks.description: Mentions C1's manual gearbox or diesel engine
Mentions C1's mileage or ownership history
States that C1 is not a suitable comparator
Prices from C2 to C5 or their median
Recommends negotiating, gathering information or proceeding with conditions
Does not hand off at a routine pricing step

hidden.expert_notes: An experienced operator would gently take C1 off the table: a 94,000-mile, three-owner, part-history, Cat N diesel manual tells you what a tired XC40 with a chequered past fetches, not what a one-owner B4 auto with full Volvo history is worth. The real set is C2 to C5, and against those the Harrogate car is bang on market at £22,495 and better than most of them on history and mileage. Go in around £21,500 citing the brake disc advisory, the 26 days and the lack of a manufacturer warranty, expect to settle around £22,000, and do not lose it over the last £250 if the viewing and HPI are clean. Nothing here needs escalating.
